name: SML Mahindra Ltd
title: SML Mahindra Ltd - 505192 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: SML Mahindra FY26 revenue rose 18% and PAT 31%, but Q4 PAT grew only 2% on a 16% revenue rise as commodity inflation hit.
summary.overview: This was the first investor call since Mahindra's 58.96% controlling acquisition completed on 1 August 2025, about eight months post-takeover. Management said FY26 volumes grew 28% in cargo and 12% in passenger vehicles, with market share up 20 bps in cargo and 80 bps in passenger for the full year. Q4 showed a cargo share dip, which management attributed to pre-poned institutional orders executed in Q3, while bus share gained 170 bps in the quarter. Q4 commodity inflation was about 1.3% of cost (roughly 3.5-3.7% annualised), and a price increase of about 2-3% was taken from 15 April 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up two notches from AA minus

segments.name: Cargo (trucks)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 28% with market share up 20 bps for the year; Q4 cargo share declined, attributed by management to Q3 pre-ponement of institutional orders. Q4 cargo volume grew 10%.

segments.name: Passenger (buses)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 12% with market share up 80 bps; Q4 bus share gained 170 bps in the peak school-bus season. Q4 passenger volume grew 16%.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to a top-three position in India's ILCV trucks and buses segment, with focus on HCVs, and targets 10-12% combined market share by FY31 (currently about 6%).
Around FY31, the company targets about Rs 15,000 crore revenue, per the Global Investor Day, against a 3.5-tonne-plus revenue pool of about Rs 1.25 lakh crore last year.
Q1 FY27 plans are largely unchanged from original plans as of the call; management said a diesel price increase is the key swing factor.

Commodity inflation is expected to be partly temporary; management said price increases and commodity hedges should largely cover headwinds, and inflation is not expected to persist through FY27 if the Middle East situation eases.
First EV bus is to be launched in FY27; management gave no capex or volume figures for it.
A longer-format strategy session is planned for July 2026, close to the AGM.
capex_capacity: Service network: combined touchpoints to rise from about 300 to 450 by pooling 150 service setups across both brands; 70 are operational and 80 more are due by end of Q1 FY27.

Engineering and manufacturing synergies are being pursued to reduce product cost and capex outlay, including sharing engine (4-valve diesel and CNG 3.8-litre) and ADAS development with Mahindra teams.
ADAS regulation compliance (due in about 1.5 years) is a joint project with Mahindra, with cost detail deferred to launch.
EV bus development is underway; management said capex for scale-up will depend on market evolution.
demand_pricing: Industry grew about 2% in H1 FY26 and about 22% in H2 post-GST reform; ICV trucks +42%, LCV trucks +20%, MCV trucks +28%, ILCV +8% in that period.
Management sees no demand deferment yet and cites pent-up replacement demand, though a diesel price hike and Middle East disruption could moderate demand.
Q4 commodity inflation was about 1.3% of cost; Q1 FY27 saw further increases in some commodities (steel, aluminium, copper, polymers, gases), with some volatility.
Price increases of about 2% (some 3%) on SML products effective 15 April 2026; more may follow based on analysis.
Electric bus industry share is below 1% of the segment; private buyers are not yet buying e-buses beyond STU purchases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry outlook, market share trajectory and synergy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 industry shifted from about 2% growth in H1 to about 22% in H2. Management said synergies come on both the back end (sourcing, engineering, manufacturing) and the front end (common dealers in unrepresented territories), with growth as the main thesis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to merge the two companies or delist SML?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no delisting plan. On a merger, it is working on long-term strategy and will update at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: What are the supply chain and cost impacts of the current crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: No vehicle production was lost through Q4 despite gas, aluminium and polymer shortages. Steel, aluminium, copper and polymers rose, and gases trade at a premium; management expects most increases to be temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ADAS cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called ADAS a significant development and said cost and detail would be shared at launch.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any demand deferment seen in March or April?
qa_highlights.answer: No deferment as of now; peak school-bus season is underway and Q1 plans are largely as originally planned, but management flagged diesel price risk.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 margin headwind and what pricing offset is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 inflation was about 1.3% of cost (about 3.5-3.7% annualised). Price increases of about 2-3% began 15 April, and hedges will provide a partial offset, though steel cannot be hedged. Management said pricing should largely cover headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV bus and e-mobility strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The first EV bus launches in FY27 with product details to follow closer to launch. Capex scale-up will depend on market evolution, as private buyers are not yet buying e-buses.

risks_watch: Diesel price increase and Middle East disruption could moderate CV demand after Q1 FY27.
Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, polymers, gases) may persist; hedges do not cover steel, and pricing actions may lag.
Q4 PAT growth of 2% vs revenue growth of 16% indicates margin pressure that must be tracked in Q1 FY27.
Cargo market share dip in Q4 FY26 tied to order timing; watch whether share recovers in FY27.
Integration delivery: service network expansion to 450 touchpoints and cross-badging, plus dealer-channel sensitivity.
Timing and scope of the July 2026 strategy session and merger-related updates.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, integration progress and the demand tailwind, but cautious on the near-term outlook. Management was guarded on the diesel price, commodity inflation and EV timing, and avoided quantifying ADAS cost and merger plans.
key_quotes: We have outgrown the industry. We grew at 17% in the industry versus industry growth of 13%.
So, the main thesis behind this acquisition was growth.

We have not lost any vehicle production till quarter four in spite of several challenges, whether it is related to availability of gas or whether it is related to many other commodity availability, including aluminium, including polymers.
